description: Capacity, throughput, latency, error counters and background maintenance for the SeaweedFS cluster (master, filer, volume servers, S3 gateway and EC workers).

panels.title: Master Leader
panels.description: 1 when the master holds the leader lock. 0 = no leader, and every write stalls cluster-wide.

panels.title: Scrape Targets Up
panels.description: SeaweedFS endpoints Prometheus is scraping successfully (master, filer, filer-client, s3, one per volume server, one per worker).

panels.title: Scrape Targets Down
panels.description: Targets that stopped responding. Above 0, the panels below are blind to part of the cluster.

panels.title: Capacity Used
panels.description: Used bytes over total bytes across every volume disk. 70% is comfortable, 85% start planning, 95% volumes flip read-only.

panels.title: Free Space
panels.description: Bytes writable across all volume disks. SeaweedFS never shrinks volumes on its own, so watch the trend.

panels.title: Under-Replicated Volumes
panels.description: Volumes with fewer copies than their replication placement (rp=001 = 2 copies). Non-zero means you are one disk failure from data loss.

panels.title: Read-Only Volumes
panels.description: Volumes flipped read-only (disk low, too many deletes, or sealed). Writes into those collections start failing.

panels.title: Disk Error Status
panels.description: Volume server disks currently in an IO error state.

panels.title: Disk Usage by Volume Server

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (pod) (SeaweedFS_volumeServer_resource{job="seaweedfs-volume", type="used", pod=~"$volume_pod"}) / sum by (pod) (SeaweedFS_volumeServer_resource{job="seaweedfs-volume", type="all", pod=~"$volume_pod"})

panels.description: Per-node disk utilisation. Volumes go read-only near 95% (or the volume server's own max), so 85%+ is the line that matters.

panels.title: Free Space by Volume Server
panels.description: Writable bytes per volume server. The master only balances new writes, so an unbalanced line stays that way until volumes are moved.

panels.title: Volumes per Server
panels.description: Volume and EC-shard counts per server. Compare against 'max volumes' when a server stops taking new volumes.

panels.title: Volume Layout — Writable vs Crowded
panels.description: The master's own view of each collection: volumes that still have room for a new needle vs volumes that are full. 0 writable = no new writes until it grows a volume.

panels.title: Space Held by Deleted Files (vacuum candidates)
panels.description: Bytes inside volumes that belong to deleted needles — exactly what a vacuum would reclaim. A line that only grows means vacuuming is not keeping up.

panels.title: Data On Disk by Collection
panels.description: How the bytes on disk are laid out per collection: `normal` replica bytes vs `ec` erasure-coded shards.

panels.title: S3 Requests by Operation
panels.description: S3 API calls per second, by HTTP verb.

panels.title: Filer Requests by Operation
panels.description: Filer calls per second — the metadata path shared by the S3 gateway and every CSI mount.

panels.title: Volume Server Requests by Operation
panels.description: Needle-level reads, writes and replica copies per second.

panels.title: Filer Request Latency
panels.description: Filer metadata latency. p99 rising while throughput stays flat usually means the metadata store (leveldb2 here) is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Volume Server Latency (p95)
panels.description: Needle read/write latency at the volume server, per operation.

panels.title: Filer Store Operations
panels.description: Operations/sec against the filer's metadata store, split by store and operation.

panels.title: In-Flight Requests
panels.description: Requests being served right now. A plateau that never drains is the signature of a stuck client or a draining worker — very different from a spiky line.

panels.title: In-Flight Upload Size
panels.description: Bytes of upload in progress right now.

panels.title: S3 Non-2xx Responses
panels.description: Every non-2xx S3 status by code and verb. 403 = credentials or policy, 404 = missing bucket/key, 500 = filer or volume trouble behind the gateway.

panels.title: Filer Non-2xx Responses
panels.description: Filer responses that are not 2xx.

panels.title: Volume Server Non-2xx Responses
panels.description: Needle requests failing at the volume server.

panels.title: Storage & IO Errors
panels.description: On-disk data integrity counters. A sustained non-zero rate is a disk or filesystem problem; invalid needles mean a read returned data that failed its own checksum.

panels.title: Master & Cluster Errors
panels.description: Master-side allocation failures (nowhere to put a new volume), cluster-wide broadcasts, and erasure-coding maintenance failures.

panels.title: Quarantined Volumes/Shards
panels.description: Volumes or EC shards quarantined after IO errors. Their data is being served from replicas only.

panels.title: Replica Placement Mismatch
panels.description: Volumes sitting on the wrong servers for their rp=001 placement. The master will try to move these.

panels.title: Read-Only S3 Buckets
panels.description: Buckets the S3 gateway has flagged read-only — usually because the collection behind them ran out of writable volumes.

panels.title: Master Disconnections (24h)
panels.description: Times a volume server lost its master connection in the last 24h. Non-zero with stable pods points at DNS or network policy trouble to the master.

panels.title: Replication Operations
panels.description: Replica writes per second by result. Only `success` should appear — anything else is a replication that did not land.

panels.title: Master Heartbeats
panels.description: Heartbeats arriving at the master (volume announcements, EC shards, data nodes). The `error` line should stay flat at zero.

panels.title: Volume → Master Connection Churn
panels.description: Failed (re)connects from SeaweedFS nodes to the master. A steady trickle means the master is unreachable from some nodes even while everything looks healthy.

panels.title: EC Vacuum Jobs
panels.description: Background erasure-coding vacuum work: jobs found, rebuilt, failed and skipped (skips usually mean the data was busy).

panels.title: EC Vacuum Bytes Reclaimed
panels.description: Rate at which the EC vacuum is returning space to the disks.

panels.title: EC Vacuum — Last Success
panels.description: When the EC vacuum last completed cleanly — the only liveness signal from the maintenance workers.

panels.title: EC Vacuum Failures (24h)
panels.description: Failed erasure-coding rebuild jobs in the last 24h.

panels.title: Filer Metadata Subscription Freshness
panels.description: Seconds since the filer last pushed a metadata update to each subscriber (S3 gateway, CSI mount, other filers). A line that grows without bound means that client is missing metadata changes; idle paths go stale naturally, so read this next to traffic.

panels.title: S3 Bucket Size (logical)
panels.description: Logical bytes per bucket, before replication.

panels.title: S3 Bucket Objects
panels.description: Object count per bucket.

panels.title: S3 Bucket Physical Size (after replication)
panels.description: Bytes actually on disk per bucket: logical size x replication (rp=001 = 2 copies) plus EC overhead.

title: SeaweedFS
